migrations.description: Sets an explicit `rootDir` on project `tsconfig*.json` files that lack one, pinned to the source directory TypeScript 5 inferred implicitly, so programs keep compiling and emitting the same layout under TypeScript 6, which otherwise hard-fails with TS5011 or TS6059 (for example a spec tsconfig importing another project's source through a `paths` alias). The pin is written even when the inferred directory already equals the tsconfig directory, because tools like ts-jest with `isolatedModules` compile a program per file and re-infer a deeper directory from that subset. The value is computed by the compiler, so emit layout is unchanged. Each config is written on its own; the migration never writes to a shared `extends` base, so a config never inherits a value computed for a sibling. Composite projects are pinned to their own directory: `rootDir` already defaults there under `tsc` so it is a no-op for a real composite build, but ts-jest strips `composite` for its per-file transpile and the explicit value is needed to avoid TS5011 there.
migrations.name: 23-1-0-set-tsconfig-root-dir-for-ts6
